newsitem.title: UK: SHELL SLIPS AS EARNINGS FALL SHORT.
newsitem.headline: SHELL SLIPS AS EARNINGS FALL SHORT.

text.p: Shares in oil group Shell Transport and Trading fell around four and a half percent on Thursday after second quarter earnings fell short of market expectations.
The shares, up 5p before the results, were 22-1/2p lower at 450-1/2p by 0910 GMT.
Ahead of the results, Shell had risen to record 480p on hopes of a positive earnings surprise, after rival British Petroleum's results exceeded expectations.
"They had a very good run ahead of these numbers, and at the end of the day it seems that BP is managing to achieve a lot more than Shell," said Peter Hitchens, oil analyst at Williams de Broe.

Royal Dutch/Shell Group said second quarter net income, excluding exceptional items fell four percent to 1.14 billion stg from 1.187 the previous year. Analysts' consensus forecast was around 1.384 billion on a current cost basis.
"The results were disappointing after the stunning set of numbers from BP," Hitchens said. "They were in line with my forecasts, which were at the bottom end of the range."
The company said that capital expenditure and costs of exploration and production were set to "step up" in the second half of the year. Shell also expected rising world crude oil output.
In a gloomy statement accompanying the results, Shell said the strength of the pound had taken its toll, with currency exchange losses of 117 million stg.
